prompt_text: I need a dental implant in Columbus. Which specific dental practices should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best dentist in Columbus Ohio for a dental implant?
answer_verbatim:
I can do this two ways: (A) give immediate steps and a few specific, reliable places you should call right away, or (B) look up local offices for you if you tell me your ZIP code or neighborhood in Columbus. Which do you prefer?

If you want immediate help now, start with these specific, high-value options and why they’re good calls:

1) The Ohio State University College of Dentistry (OSU Dental Clinics) — call the prosthodontics/oral surgery clinics
- Why: University clinics treat a high volume of complex cases, faculty are specialists (prosthodontists/oral surgeons/periodontists), care is supervised by experienced professors, and costs are often lower than private specialists. Good if you want a second opinion or a more affordable option.

2) An oral & maxillofacial surgery practice (search “oral & maxillofacial surgeon Columbus”)
- Why: OMS surgeons place implants and handle surgical complexity (bone grafting, extractions, sinus lifts, IV sedation). Call an OMS if you expect surgical complexity or sedation needs.

3) A periodontist who does implants (search “periodontist dental implants Columbus”)
- Why: Periodontists specialize in the gums and bone and focus on implant placement and bone regeneration—excellent for patients needing gum/bone work and esthetic implant results.

4) A prosthodontist or multidisciplinary implant center (search “prosthodontist Columbus” or “implant center Columbus”)
- Why: Prosthodontists design the crowns/bridges that go on implants and manage complex full-arch restorations. Multidisciplinary centers coordinate surgeon + restorative dentist under one roof for smoother care.

How to find specific doctors in Columbus (quickly and reliably)
- Use these directories: AAOMS.org (oral surgeons), AAP.org (periodontists), AAID.org or ACP.org (prosthodontists), and Google/Healthgrades/Yelp for local reviews. Look for “Fellow” or “Board Certified” on profiles.
- Check the OSU College of Dentistry website for specialty clinic phone numbers.

What to ask when you call (use this script)
- Do you place dental implants on-site? Who places the implant and who does the final crown restoration?
- How many implant cases like mine do you do per year? Do you place implants for single-tooth, multiple, or full-arch restorations?
- Do you use CBCT (3D CT) for planning and do you offer guided surgery?
- Will bone grafting or sinus lift be needed? If so, is it done here?
- Which implant systems/brands do you use?
- What sedation options are available (local, oral sedative, IV)?
- Can you give a written estimate and a breakdown (surgery, implant, abutment, crown)?
- Do you accept my insurance? Do you offer financing?
- What is your complication/warranty policy for implants?

Red flags to avoid
- No CBCT or no ability to refer for 3D imaging for planning complex cases.
- Surgeon/dentist can’t say their experience level or number of implants placed.
- Vague, no-itemized cost estimate or unwillingness to provide options (single implant vs grafting vs alternative).
- Poor online reviews citing implant failures or poor follow-up care.

If you want, give me your ZIP code or neighborhood and I’ll list 4–6 specific Columbus practices (with phone suggestions and which one to call first depending on whether you need simple single-tooth implant vs full-arch work).
